units.title: Unit 25 — Commuting
learningObjectives: Describe commuting routes, ticketing and service disruption with natural combinations.
Discuss transport policy, congestion and road-management solutions precisely.
Distinguish neutral fare changes from emphatic price hikes and recognise common transport notices.

items.example: The village has poor local transport links, so many residents rely on cars.
items.note: Transport links connect places through available routes and services.

items.pt: rota utilizada por quem se desloca diariamente ao trabalho
items.example: The main commuter route becomes congested before eight every morning.
items.note: A commuter route serves regular journeys between home and work.

items.example: Drivers often get stuck in traffic near the bridge at dawn.
items.note: Get stuck in traffic describes being delayed because vehicles are barely moving.

items.example: We took the toll road to avoid the slower coastal highway.
items.note: A toll road charges drivers for using it, often in return for a faster route.

items.example: Cycling is sometimes faster than driving during rush hour.
items.note: Rush hour is a period of especially heavy travel demand.

items.pt: trem usado por passageiros que viajam regularmente
items.example: An early commuter train carries office workers into the capital.
items.note: Commuter trains generally serve repeated journeys into and out of work centres.

items.pt: passe de transporte válido por um período
items.example: Her annual season ticket costs less than buying individual fares.
items.note: A season ticket allows repeated travel for a fixed period on an eligible service.

items.pt: viajar no horário de maior movimento
items.example: Employees who travel at peak time rarely find empty seats.
items.note: Peak time is the busiest period and may carry higher fares.

items.pt: viagem fora do horário de pico
items.example: Off-peak travel can be considerably cheaper on regional trains.
items.note: Off-peak contrasts with peak-time travel and may involve fare restrictions.

items.pt: obras de manutenção ou reparo na ferrovia
items.example: Weekend engineering works will close two platforms at the station.
items.note: In British rail announcements, engineering works means planned maintenance or repairs.

items.example: Passengers used a replacement bus service while the track was repaired.
items.note: A replacement bus service operates when the normal train service is unavailable.

items.pt: rede de ciclovias e rotas para bicicletas
items.example: The council expanded the cycle network to connect suburban districts.
items.note: A cycle network is a connected system of routes intended for cycling.

items.pt: faixas exclusivas ou sinalizadas para bicicletas
items.example: New cycle lanes separate bicycles from fast-moving vehicles.
items.note: Cycle lanes are marked parts of roads reserved or designated for cyclists.

items.example: A breakdown near the tunnel caused traffic gridlock across the district.
items.note: Gridlock is an extreme traffic jam in which movement becomes almost impossible.

items.example: The former farming village is now a busy commuter town outside the city.
items.note: A commuter town is a residential town from which many people travel elsewhere to work.

items.example: The region invested heavily in its bus and rail network.
items.note: Bus and rail network groups two coordinated forms of public transport.

items.example: Regular passengers have complained about overcrowded trains on the northern line.
items.note: Overcrowded signals that a train contains more passengers than is comfortable or safe.

items.example: Packed trains force some commuters to stand for the entire journey.
items.note: Packed trains emphasises that very little room remains for passengers.

items.example: Repeated fare rises have made the monthly journey less affordable.
items.note: Fare refers to the price of a journey; rises describes increases in that price.

items.example: Several train strikes disrupted services during the negotiations.
items.note: A train strike involves rail staff stopping work as part of industrial action.

items.example: The city plans to invest in infrastructure rather than expand car parking.
items.note: Invest in is followed by the sector or facilities receiving investment.

items.example: Rural communities need reliable local transport services after dark.
items.note: This combination refers to buses, trains or other transport serving nearby areas.

items.example: A hike in fares prompted complaints from regular passengers.
items.note: A hike implies a noticeable or steep increase, stronger than a neutral rise.

items.example: The morning express is running late because of a signalling failure.
items.note: Running late is standard for delayed scheduled services, including trains and buses.

items.example: Flexible working hours could ease traffic congestion on the ring road.
items.note: Ease traffic congestion means make heavy traffic less severe, not remove it entirely.

items.example: The transport plan aims to reduce private car use in the centre.
items.note: Private car use contrasts with travel by shared or public transport.

items.pt: programas de compartilhamento de carros ou caronas
items.example: The university introduced car-sharing programmes for staff in nearby towns.
items.note: Car-sharing programmes encourage people to share vehicle access or journeys; the model depends on context.

items.pt: sistemas de estacionamento integrado ao transporte público
items.example: New park-and-ride schemes let drivers finish their journey by tram.
items.note: Park-and-ride combines parking outside a busy centre with public transport onward.

items.pt: taxa de circulação em área congestionada
items.example: The mayor proposed a congestion charge for vehicles entering the business district.
items.note: A congestion charge is paid for driving into a designated zone, not for parking.

items.example: The region reviewed its road-building programmes after costs increased.
items.note: Road-building programmes are coordinated projects for constructing or expanding roads.

items.pt: reduzir os pontos de estrangulamento do tráfego
items.example: Changing the junction layout should alleviate bottlenecks at the tunnel entrance.
items.note: A bottleneck is a narrow or overloaded point that slows the wider traffic flow.

items.example: Temporary road closures will protect runners during the city marathon.
items.note: Road closures are periods when roads are closed to some or all traffic.

items.example: An overturned lorry produced lengthy tailbacks on both sides of the motorway.
items.note: Tailbacks are queues of vehicles stretching back from an obstruction; lengthy stresses distance.

items.example: A major power failure could bring traffic to a standstill at busy intersections.
items.note: Bring traffic to a standstill means cause vehicles to stop moving completely.

items.example: Peak-time delays affected thousands of passengers on Monday morning.
items.note: Peak-time identifies the period affected; delays are disruptions to the schedule.

items.example: The government will modernise the rail network over the next decade.
items.note: A rail network consists of connected railway routes and their supporting system.

items.example: Passengers objected to a rise in fares on the regional railway.
items.note: A rise in fares is neutral, whereas a hike in fares emphasises size.

items.example: Regional leaders promised to improve road and rail links between remote towns.
items.note: Road and rail links are routes connecting places by highway or railway.

units.title: Unit 26 — Travel and adventure
learningObjectives: Use natural language for travel motivation, route planning and challenging journeys.
Describe wilderness experiences, weather and expedition problems accurately.
Choose idiomatic combinations for budgets, journey stages and travellers’ emotional reactions.

items.example: A thirst for adventure took her well beyond familiar tourist routes.
items.note: A thirst for adventure is a figurative strong desire to explore new experiences.

items.pt: sentir vontade de viajar ou mudar de lugar
items.example: After a year in one city, I began to get itchy feet again.
items.note: Get itchy feet is an informal idiom for becoming restless and wanting to move or travel.

items.example: I could barely contain my excitement when the expedition was approved.
items.note: Contain excitement means control a strong positive emotional reaction.

items.example: We set off for the national park just before sunrise.
items.note: Set off for introduces the destination when a journey begins.

items.example: They completed an arduous journey across the mountains in freezing rain.
items.note: Arduous stresses that a trip is physically or mentally demanding.

items.example: We decided to break the journey overnight in a small seaside town.
items.note: Break the journey means pause a long trip before travelling on.

items.example: Driving across the country in one go would leave us exhausted.
items.note: In one go means without splitting the action into separate stages.

items.pt: fazer uma parada intermediária na viagem
items.example: We will have a stopover in Lisbon before continuing to Morocco.
items.note: A stopover is a planned intermediate stay, commonly on a longer flight itinerary.

items.example: We had an afternoon free to do the sights before our evening flight.
items.note: Do the sights is informal British English for visiting major attractions.

items.example: A low-cost airline offered cheaper tickets but charged for luggage.
items.note: A low-cost airline typically offers basic fares with optional paid extras.

items.pt: colocar na lista de espera por uma vaga
items.example: The agent put us on standby for the last flight of the day.
items.note: Passengers on standby wait to see whether a seat becomes available.

items.pt: fazer trilhas longas ou caminhadas de aventura
items.example: They plan to go trekking in the hills during their holiday.
items.note: Go trekking means travel on foot over long or challenging routes.

items.example: The guide introduced us to a village well off the beaten track.
items.note: This idiom describes places away from usual tourist routes.

items.example: The documentary follows an intrepid explorer through remote valleys.
items.note: Intrepid suggests courage in unfamiliar or potentially dangerous conditions.

items.example: The maps showed a vast area of unexplored wilderness beyond the river.
items.note: Wilderness refers to uncultivated land; unexplored stresses little prior investigation.

items.example: A strong sense of adventure encouraged them to change their plans.
items.note: Sense of adventure is an attitude of curiosity and readiness for novel experiences.

items.example: Without a working compass, the hikers soon became hopelessly lost.
items.note: Hopelessly intensifies lost: finding the way back seems extremely difficult.

items.example: A search party found the missing climbers before nightfall.
items.note: A search party is a group organised to locate missing people.

items.example: Forecasters expect sunny spells between the afternoon showers.
items.note: Sunny spells are intervals of sunshine, usually between cloudy periods.

items.example: A warm meal helped boost spirits after the difficult descent.
items.note: Boost spirits means improve the mood or confidence of a group; a possessive can specify whose.

items.example: The research team may face severe weather conditions near the summit.
items.note: Face conditions expresses having to deal with difficult circumstances.

items.example: The expedition returned safely to base camp before the storm arrived.
items.note: A base camp is a main support site for a longer expedition.

items.example: Despite the delays, spirits are high among the volunteers.
items.note: This fixed pattern reports that a group feels cheerful or optimistic.

items.example: The epic grandeur of the canyon surprised even experienced travellers.
items.note: Epic grandeur conveys a vast and awe-inspiring scale in descriptions of scenery.

items.example: The old fishing port has a special charm at sunset.
items.note: Special charm describes an appealing character that makes something distinctive.

items.example: Keep your eyes peeled for wildlife near the marshes.
items.note: Informal expression meaning remain highly alert and look carefully.

items.pt: o orçamento não é suficiente para
items.example: Our budget does not stretch to a private cabin on the ship.
items.note: Stretch to means be sufficient to pay for a particular expense.

items.example: You can curl up in your seat during an overnight journey.
items.note: Curl up describes adopting a compact resting position in a seat.

items.example: The rhythmic motion of the ferry made several passengers sleepy.
items.note: Rhythmic motion describes regular, repeated movement.

items.example: The steady sound of rain might lull you to sleep.
items.note: Lull someone to sleep means gently cause them to become sleepy.

items.example: The first leg of the journey took us through coastal villages.
items.note: A leg is a distinct stage in a journey with several parts.

items.example: We cannot predict what lies ahead beyond the next mountain pass.
items.note: What lies ahead refers to events or difficulties still to come.

items.example: Aerial photographs revealed a stretch of unexplored territory inland.
items.note: Unexplored territory is land that has not been thoroughly investigated.

items.pt: passagem sujeita à disponibilidade de lugar
items.example: A standby ticket was cheaper but did not guarantee a seat.
items.note: Standby tickets depend on spare seats becoming available.

items.pt: fazendo travessia a pé pelas montanhas
items.example: The group spent a fortnight trekking through the mountains.
items.note: Through the mountains describes the terrain crossed during a trek.

items.example: The arduous climb demanded frequent stops for water.
items.note: Arduous combines naturally with demanding activities such as climbs or tasks.

items.pt: águas desconhecidas ou território novo em sentido figurado
items.example: Launching the new research programme took the team into uncharted waters.
items.note: Uncharted waters is literal for unmapped seas and figurative for unfamiliar situations.

items.example: The expedition crossed uncharted territory beyond the mapped valley.
items.note: Uncharted territory has both geographic and figurative uses for unfamiliar areas.

items.example: Severe weather conditions forced the organisers to postpone the hike.
items.note: Severe strengthens the description of hazardous or difficult weather.
